papers.title_en: Live Assistant: Learning Whether, When, and Whom to Assist in Real-World Live Social Streams
papers.authors: Shujian Gao, Jiamei Yan, Yuchen Yang, Penghao Zhou, Qinglei Wang, Tiehan Fan, Yuan Wang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-gang Jiang
papers.evidence: 混合主动前瞻式协助，实时决定是否、何时、向谁介入
papers.tldr: 直播中音视频、观众行为、主播与平台信号持续演化，助手介入需求随流涌现。论文提出 LiveAssistant，将直播交互建模为是否行动、何时行动、面向谁、说什么四个耦合决策，每10秒基于多模态信号自回归选择 OBS/MEM/ANS。作者构建轨迹引擎与人工复核基准，用 MA-MSFT 和 SM-GSPO 训练策略。基准上状态、对象、任务准确率达71.14、72.67、58.41，确立直播助手为共享社交流中的选择性参与。
papers.abstract_en: Livestreams are long-lasting interactive environments where audiovisual content, viewer activity, host behavior, and platform signals evolve together, creating assistance needs that emerge from the stream itself. We introduce \liveassistant, a framework for mixed-initiative, role-conditioned assistance that formulates livestream interaction as four coupled decisions: \textbf{whether to act, when to act, whom to address, and what to communicate}. At each 10-second interval, one autoregressive policy consumes native audio and video with synchronized comments, gifts, viewer dynamics, and room metadata, then selects \textsc{OBS}, \textsc{MEM}, or \textsc{ANS}. \textsc{OBS} remains silent, \textsc{MEM} records a private semantic update, and \textsc{ANS} specifies a recipient, task, and grounded message. To support this task, we build a trajectory engine that reconstructs real livestream sessions into structured causal supervision, yielding over 320 hours of optimization trajectories and a human-reviewed benchmark of 275 clips and 13,812 decision intervals. We train the policy with Marker-Aware Multiturn Supervised Fine-Tuning (MA-MSFT), which strengthens sparse structured decisions, followed by Streaming Multiturn GSPO (SM-GSPO), which optimizes self-generated trajectories with turn- and trajectory-level credit. On the held-out benchmark, \liveassistant reaches 71.14 state accuracy, 72.67 recipient accuracy, and 58.41 task accuracy, with consistent gains over representative streaming and general multimodal baselines. Together, the formulation, benchmark, and training framework establish livestream assistance as selective participation in a shared social stream.

papers.title_en: Clarify the User or Verify the World? Uncertainty Routing for Proactive Agents
papers.authors: Zhaofeng Li, Xuan Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Yang Deng
papers.evidence: 对用户目标解释的主动不确定性路由
papers.tldr: 工具型LLM智能体需判断是否补充信息，并选择向用户澄清还是验证环境。现有主动方法多只擅长单一来源，难以按决策路由。PROUR将动作不确定性分解为用户目标解释间分歧与解释内熵，分别指示CLARIFY和VERIFY，并用模式条件信息增益奖励训练查询生成器。在τ-bench上平均成功率28.17%，较最强基线提升4.57%且少用2.17步，并零样本泛化到τ^3-bench。
papers.abstract_en: Tool-using LLM agents must decide not only whether additional information is needed, but also which source can resolve the uncertainty. Existing proactive approaches often specialize in either user clarification or environment verification, without explicitly determining the appropriate information source for each decision. We formulate this problem as uncertainty routing among ACT, CLARIFY, and VERIFY, and propose PROUR, a proactive uncertainty routing framework. PROUR decomposes action uncertainty into disagreement across plausible user-goal interpretations, which signals user-side ambiguity, and the entropy remaining within each interpretation, which signals missing world-side evidence. To acquire information from the routed source, a query generator is trained with a mode-conditioned information-gain reward, targeting user-goal identification under CLARIFY and next-action identification under VERIFY. On $τ$-bench, PROUR achieves 28.17% average success rate across retail and airline, outperforming the strongest prior method by 4.57% while using 2.17 fewer interaction steps. The learned policy further generalizes to stronger task agents and transactional domains of $τ^3$-bench without retraining, demonstrating the benefit of source-aligned uncertainty resolution for proactive agents.
